content:
Since \(A\) is finite, an onto function \(\pi:A\to A\) must be a permutation. Write \(\pi\) as a product of disjoint cycles.

The condition
\[
\pi^6(a)=a\qquad\text{for all }a\in A
\]
means that the order of \(\pi\) divides \(6\). Thus every cycle length must divide \(6\). The possible cycle lengths are therefore
\[
1,2,3,6.
\]

For a cycle type having \(m_\ell\) cycles of length \(\ell\), the number of permutations of six elements with that type is
\[
\frac{6!}{\prod_\ell \ell^{m_\ell}m_\ell!}.
\]

We list all partitions of \(6\) using only \(1,2,3,6\):

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{Cycle type} & \text{Number of permutations}\\ \hline
(6) & \frac{6!}{6}=120\\[2mm]
(3,3) & \frac{6!}{3^2\cdot 2!}=40\\[2mm]
(3,2,1) & \frac{6!}{3\cdot2}=120\\[2mm]
(3,1,1,1) & \frac{6!}{3\cdot3!}=40\\[2mm]
(2,2,2) & \frac{6!}{2^3\cdot3!}=15\\[2mm]
(2,2,1,1) & \frac{6!}{2^2\cdot2!\cdot2!}=45\\[2mm]
(2,1,1,1,1) & \frac{6!}{2\cdot4!}=15\\[2mm]
(1,1,1,1,1,1) & 1
\end{array}
\]

Therefore, the total number is
\[
120+40+120+40+15+45+15+1=396.
\]

\[
\boxed{396}
\]
